title: Pool kinds and what they cost

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, why can `Executors.newCachedThreadPool()` run out of memory under sustained load?

options.text: Its waiting tasks pile up in a queue that has no capacity limit
options.says: The page says the queue without a limit belongs to newFixedThreadPool; the cached pool's SynchronousQueue holds no tasks at all.

options.text: Its idle threads stay alive and are never taken back by the pool
options.says: The page says the cached pool reuses idle threads and reclaims them after 60 seconds.

options.text: Its thread count has no upper bound, so busy periods add more threads
options.says: The page says its maximum pool size is Integer.MAX_VALUE, so it starts a thread whenever all are busy, and each platform thread holds about 1MB of stack.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does switching a service that sends thousands of HTTP calls from `newFixedThreadPool(200)` to `newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` improve?

options.text: The number of requests the service can have in flight together
options.says: The page's Q6 example shows only 200 requests in flight with the fixed pool and all 10,000 at once with virtual threads, which it calls more scalable.

options.text: The time each single request takes from being sent to its reply
options.says: The page says virtual threads do NOT make your code faster; they make it more scalable by allowing many more concurrent tasks.

options.text: The rate at which requests that compute on the CPU get finished
options.says: The page says virtual threads are NOT beneficial for CPU-bound workloads, since they share carrier threads.

concepts: newCachedThreadPool() has no bound on its threads, so sustained load can create thousands of them and exhaust memory.
Virtual threads let far more I/O-bound tasks wait at once, but they do not make any single task faster.
